{"id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-06hw","title":"accept/compress keep superseded DIO SCHC policy live","description":"File: rust/lichen-schc/src/link.rs

compress_schc_for_peer and accept_authenticated_schc_packet gate only on peer.is_current_for(link) (DIO evidence still accepted by this LinkLayer: same receiver Arc, current key-generation Arc, still pinned). That is not 'latest DIO for this signer'.

PeerContextAuthority::issue_from_authenticated_dio and FragmentationPolicy::install_peer both reject authenticated_counter <= the stored floor and bump generation so an older capability fails is_current/accepts_entry. from_authenticated_dio_frame (the only constructor that sets evidence, which is_current_for requires) has no such registry. A later DIO for the same signer (higher seqnum, possibly incompatible Rule Set Version) leaves the earlier AuthenticatedPeerSchcContext fully usable:

- compress_schc_for_peer still encodes under the old remote_version (v3 compressed rules after a mismatch DIO, or the reverse)
- accept_authenticated_schc_packet still decompresses data with counter > the OLD floor under the old policy, even when a newer DIO admitted a stricter floor and different version

Python LinkLayer keeps one _schc_peer_contexts entry per signer and always looks that up (w0mm is the store-rollback dual). Std link.rs has no equivalent, so stale and current capabilities both work until unpin/rekey.

Fix: keep a per-signer latest DIO counter/version (PeerContextAuthority, FragmentationPolicy, or LinkLayer) and treat a context as current only when its authenticated_counter/generation is the live one. Reject superseded contexts as InvalidPeerEvidence. The seqnum-20 context still compresses/accepts. If the second DIO advertises an incompatible Rule Set Version, data is not decompressed with v3 compressed rules via the first context. FragmentationPolicy/PeerContextAuthority supersession behavior is unchanged. new_value: {"notes":"2026-08-26 Phase-2 fix: added bounded 32-entry AuthenticatedSchcPolicy owner for std link integration. compress_schc_for_peer and accept_authenticated_schc_packet now require the candidate context to match the registry's signer/counter/version/key-generation entry before output or policy use. DIO role is cryptographically parsed then retained in AuthenticatedPeerSchcContext, so callers cannot mislabel root vs peer. Same-signer refresh/version change supersedes older capabilities; \u003c= counter and receipt-clock rollback reject; a different authenticated root becomes current while the old root high-water remains retained, preventing rollback when switching back. Regression encodes the prior seq10 context surviving seq20 failure mode and covers old/new acceptance+compression, same-version refresh, v3-to-incompatible fallback, root switch, rollback before/after switch, and output non-mutation. Existing 2tdl destination filtering preserved. Green: focused lifecycle test; full lichen-schc std suite (71 unit, all integrations/vectors/docs, 7 link integration); strict std all-target Clippy; no-default-features check; targeted rustfmt and diff checks. C/Zephyr audit found wire codecs and rule-version option parsing but no retained std peer-capability/free-function analog, so no west build was applicable. No Phase-3 review."}
Bound std SCHC compression/ingress to the latest authenticated signer/version/root policy with rollback-safe tests and green scoped gates.
